title: The Cover of the DMZ
premise: Silas Kavanagh, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Liaison Office — an embassy that exists on no map — is confronted by a woman named Ada Reyes who claims he saved her life in Panmunjom five years ago. He has no memory of it, but her debt comes with a ledger: a dead courier's microfilm hidden inside the DMZ's Joint Security Area, evidence of a trilateral arms deal that three governments will kill to bury. As Silas and Ada cross borders both literal and psychological, Silas discovers his 'missing' memory was surgically taken, and that he himself helped design the cover-up he's now fighting. In the end, Silas chooses to burn his own identity to get the truth out, broadcasting the ledger from inside the DMZ as the assassin closes in — surviving as no one at all.
about_author: Freya Pemberton is a former diplomatic interpreter who spent six years posted along contested border zones before turning to fiction full-time. She writes thrillers about people whose loyalties are written in pencil, and lives between two countries she refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Silas Kavanagh's POV. A routine night of cleaning up an ambassador's indiscretion establishes his world: forged passports, polished lies, a bag always packed. He returns to his flat to find it untouched yet subtly wrong — someone has been inside and left nothing but a matchbook from Panmunjom. Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Silas POV. Ada Reyes corners him in a tram station, thanking him for saving her life in the DMZ five years ago — a date he spent, he knows, in a hospital with no memories. She says the debt is owed with interest and slides him a key. He denies everything; she expected him to. Beat: vertigo of a past that doesn't fit.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada POV. She explains: a courier died carrying microfilm documenting a secret trilateral weapons transfer routed through the Joint Security Area. The hiding place is keyed to the matchbook. She needs a man who can move through the Meridian Liaison Office's blind spots — Silas. Beat: reluctant bargain struck over fear.

chapters.title: Office of No One
chapters.summary: Silas POV. He probes his own agency's archives for the incident date and finds his file redacted by his own handprint — authorization codes only he could have used, from days he cannot remember. His handler, Voss, watches him too closely. Beat: the enemy may be wearing his own face.

chapters.title: Crossing at Dusk
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Silas and Ada enter the DMZ under cover of a maintenance convoy, tension high as patrols sweep close. They reach the cache point and find it already opened — emptied recently, deliberately, with a taunting note left behind. Beat: hope curdling into pursuit.

chapters.title: The Man Who Waits
chapters.summary: Assassin Corvin's POV, first appearance. Elegant, patient, he reports to an unnamed principal that the ledger is recovered — but he kept a copy, insurance against employers who burn tools. He identifies Silas as the loose thread. Beat: cold menace; the hunter has his own agenda.

chapters.title: Redacted
chapters.summary: Silas POV. Fleeing north, Silas finds a private clinic in his old files — records of an elective memory excision, signed by himself. Ada realizes he didn't lose the past; he amputated it. Their trust fractures. Beat: betrayal without a betrayer.

chapters.title: What Ada Knows
chapters.summary: Ada POV. Flashback chapter: the real events five years ago — Silas, pre-wipe, saving her during the courier's death, telling her 'if I come back wrong, finish this.' She reveals she chose him not despite the missing memory but because of it. Beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Voss POV. The Liaison Office, Korean intelligence, and a shadowed American contingent all converge on the pair. Voss, torn, quietly delays the kill order — Silas was the best fixer she ever ran, and she suspects what was done to him. Beat: loyalty as quiet rebellion.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Silas POV. Holed up in Osaka, they reconstruct the deal from fragments: the ledger names a sitting minister, a general, and — devastatingly — the architect of the cover-up protocol. The signature matches Silas's own design work. Beat: self-loathing sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Corvin's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvin POV then confrontation. He intercepts them, but instead of killing Silas offers partnership: his copy of the ledger for passage out, since his employers plan to erase him next. Ada doesn't trust it; Silas recognizes a man keeping a go-bag packed. Beat: uneasy triangle of survivors.

chapters.title: The Minister's Dinner
chapters.summary: Silas POV. An infiltration of a diplomatic reception to confirm the minister's involvement goes wrong when Silas is recognized by someone from his forgotten life — a colleague who greets him by a different name. Beat: identity cracking open in public.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Ada POV. The colleague, Marta, tells them who Silas was before the wipe: the author of the erasure program itself, who volunteered as its first subject out of guilt after the courier died. Ada must reconcile the man she owes with the man he chose to stop being. Beat: compassion over judgment.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Silas POV. The Office declares Silas rogue; assets freeze, safehouses close, Voss is ordered to deliver him. She instead passes him one last asset — a route into the DMZ during a scheduled joint inspection. Beat: the net tightening even as a door opens.

chapters.title: Corvin's Price
chapters.summary: Corvin POV. His employers attempt to eliminate him; he survives by a hair and burns his own network in retaliation, going fully off-book. He sends Silas a single message: the inspection window, and 'bring the truth or don't bother.' Beat: hunter becomes fellow fugitive.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Costs
chapters.summary: Ada POV. Preparing for the final run, Ada confesses her own stake: the courier was her brother, and the 'favor' story was her way in — though the gratitude became real. Silas, instead of rage, offers partnership of equals. Beat: honesty as the only currency left.

chapters.title: Into the Zone
chapters.summary: Silas POV. The trio infiltrates the JSA during the joint inspection, moving through the blue-roofed buildings as dignitaries pose for cameras meters away. Corvin draws off a patrol at terrible cost, buying them minutes. Beat: breathless, surgical tension.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In a sealed sub-basement, they find the original archive — and Voss waiting, gun raised, ordered to stop them. Silas talks her down using her own delayed kill orders as proof she never believed either. She turns, becoming their witness. Beat: standoff resolved by truth-telling.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Silas POV. From inside the DMZ's communication suite, they push the ledger to every press desk and archive mirror simultaneously. Alarms scream; Corvin, wounded, holds the corridor. The assassin's last act is holding the door. Beat: triumphant, costly climax.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Ledger
chapters.summary: Corvin POV, final chapter of his arc. Dying, he reflects that he finally kept a promise to himself. His copy reaches a journalist posthumously, ensuring redundancy. Beat: elegy for a professional who chose a side at the end.

chapters.title: No One at All
chapters.summary: Silas POV. Exposed and officially erased, Silas surrenders his identities entirely — new face of the investigation, nameless witness statements, no country. Ada finds him weeks later in a border town; he doesn't ask to be remembered. Beat: freedom through self-annihilation.

chapters.title: The Cover of the DMZ
chapters.summary: Ada POV, coda. Months later, hearings ripple through three capitals; the minister falls. Ada visits the JSA as a tourist, places the matchbook on the bridge rail, and walks away. Somewhere, a man with no name watches her go and lets her. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
